newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Battered Australian bonds left guessing on US.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Battered Australian bonds left guessing on US.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs after another day of aggressive swings as the market continued to be battered by events offshore.
*U.S. releases November CPI and retail trade later today.
Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs after another day of aggressive swings as the market continued to be battered by events offshore.
Domestic institutions saved the day from a rout, picking up cheap stock after U.S. funds sold the market off in tandem with a plunge in U.S. Treasuries.

"After hours offshore selling spilled over into the morning and continued right up until today's figure (employment)," said one trader. "Sentiment has turned about face and people are now looking to sell into rallies."
The market was pretty much left guessing over the next move.

The U.S. releases November CPI and retail sales later today which could set the local tone for Friday, although Thursday's publication of the PPI was all but ignored as the market was more anxious over future participation by Japanese investors.

Such demand was put in doubt by U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs who saw it tapering off due to the U.S.'s trade imbalances. Meanwhile, today's Australian labour force data was stronger than expected at first glance, but a 24,000 employment rise was largely made up of part-time workers, and the fall in unemployment to 8.5 percent was seen being short-lived.
Today's local weak tone wiped out Wednesday's rally at the long end which followed the surprise cut in official interest rates to 6.0 percent by the Reserve Bank.

Analysts appear to be fairly split as to whether the central bank will go ease again, and some believe that it may have gone too far already to beef up growth, which could damage the positive inflation outlook.
Rates were cut to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent. Monetary policy has been eased three times since mid-year, with the latest easing based on a good inflation outlook.
Local long bonds underperformed the rest of the dollar bloc, with Canada and New Zealand debt both taking their leads from the U.S.
The local yield curve extended Wednesday's steepening with the short-end protected by the surprise rate cut by the RBA.
